assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a single artificial atom and a single microwave photon strongly coupled and fully controllable on a chip, opening a new regime of light-matter interaction in solid-state circuits. It is the enabling platform for dispersive readout, microwave quantum optics and superconducting quantum processors, and follows naturally from the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits. The physics is clean, with every detail understood.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the 2004 theory proposal, Schoelkopf's Yale group (with Wallraff as lead experimentalist) delivered the 2004 strong-coupling demonstration, and Wallraff later built an independent programme at ETH. The three credited names form a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration. Credit for the transmon and for Devoret-group contributions lies partly outside this trio and the 2025 prize, so the boundary needs care.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and extended across dozens of laboratories for twenty years, and now the dominant superconducting-qubit architecture. Recognition is timely and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may be seen as too close, though the discovery (strong light-matter coupling) is distinct from macroscopic tunnelling.
Whether theory credit should include Girvin or Huang, who are not in the supplied credited names, is unresolved.
As a member working in this field I may be biased and should defer on conflict-of-interest questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cooling mechanical oscillators to their quantum ground state and controlling them with light or microwaves (sideband cooling, squeezing, entanglement, ponderomotive correlations) brought mesoscopic massive objects into the quantum regime. This is a genuine new regime, demonstrated with clear and controllable experiments that connect to quantum sensing and transduction.
assessment.attribution: Teufel (microwave circuit electromechanics, ground-state cooling 2011), Aspelmeyer (cavity optomechanics, entanglement and macroscopic quantum states) and Kippenberg (sideband cooling, microresonator platforms) are plausible central figures. Cleland and Painter made equally important results (first quantum ground state of a mechanical resonator, optomechanical crystals), so excluding them is a real fairness concern with five credited names.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent groups have reproduced the main milestones over more than a decade. The field is mature, though the applications such as transduction are still developing.
uncertainties: Choice of three among five strongly deserving names is difficult and contested.
Priority between Cleland's 2010 piezoelectric qubit-resonator result and the optomechanical cooling results is open.
I have not verified the exact first-demonstration dates and rely on memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials as a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. Originality and impact are very high, with a new class of tunable quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theory prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the 2018 experiments. Credit for the experimental discovery of the correlated phases in 2018 is shared with others in the Jarillo-Herrero group, and the clean three-name split is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced widely since 2018, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated states is still debated and the field is young. Recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Sample dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility.
Other contributors to the experimental discovery are not in the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the Cirac-Zoller and Jaksch proposals to the observation of the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes, gives controllable emulation of Hubbard-type models. It is a genuine platform where basic many-body quantum phenomena can be seen and tuned.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied key theory proposals (with Jaksch and Cirac), Bloch and Greiner carried out the decisive experiments (Mott transition 2002, microscopes). Cirac is also credited and has an equally strong theoretical claim, so the omission of one theorist is a trade-off. Hanns-Christoph Haensch's lattice work is also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Well established, widely replicated, and heavily used. Practical quantum advantage in simulation is still being explored, but the discovery itself is mature.
uncertainties: Which theorist, Cirac or Zoller, should be recognised alongside the experimentalists is not clear.
Overlap with B019, B031 and B036, which share Zoller and Cirac, could fragment the case across candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum measurement and entanglement into a protocol with provable security, and has been realised from lab bench to fibre and satellite links. Conceptual originality is high (BB84, E91), and the discovery is the foundational protocol rather than the technology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard created BB84 and Ekert E91, which ties to Bell tests. Jian-Wei Pan led later experimental networks but the foundational credit is clearest with the first three. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a known attribution issue.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated many times, but practical security against side-channel attacks and real-world deployment remain debated. The foundational concept is mature even if the technology is not.
uncertainties: Whether the Academy sees this as physics or as computer science and cryptography.
Wiesner's prior contribution and the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments may weigh on priority and overlap.
I defer partly to colleagues on cryptographic security claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping, reached fractional uncertainties around 1e-18 and enabled tests of relativity at the millimetre scale and prospects for a redefinition of the second. It is a clean, robust instrument-driven advance with an unambiguous new precision regime.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2001-2003 and Ye achieved the leading experimental realisations and precision. Two laureates are a fair configuration, though earlier ion-clock work (Wineland, 2012) and the Hall-Haensch comb recognition form context.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many laboratories with agreement at the 1e-18 level. Recognition would be timely, but the redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Overlap with Hall and Haensch (2005) and Wineland (2012) may be seen as incremental by some members.
Whether others who contributed the key magic-wavelength ideas should share credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new topological classification of band insulators with protected edge states. Impact on condensed-matter physics has been very large.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, Molenkamp's group the first experimental observation (with Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang proposing HgTe). Hasan is credited for 3D topological insulators. The configuration is hard because of the Zhang death and parallel contributions, and Thouless-Haldane-Kosterlitz (2016) already recognised topological phases.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed experimentally across many materials, but the 2016 prize overlap makes timing and novelty arguments difficult.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.
Credit for HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is outside the supplied names.
I defer to condensed-matter colleagues on materials priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum computation with trapped ions and its experimental implementation made individually controlled quantum bits and entangling gates a reality, and underpin a major quantum-computing platform with extremely high fidelity.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal and Blatt's group demonstrated key algorithms and gates, though Wineland and Monroe (NIST) demonstrated the first gate. Wineland already has a prize, and Monroe is not in the credited list, so the credit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Highly reproduced and mature, but practical fault-tolerant scale-up is still ahead and the discovery boundary is blurred relative to the Wineland recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with B031 and B034, with the same credited trio.
Omission of Monroe and the NIST group may be seen as unfair.
Fault-tolerant scaling remains unproven.
